tiers.do: Step outside your front door. Stand there for sixty seconds. Go back in.
tiers.why: You are not going anywhere today. You are proving the door opens.
tiers.alt: Open a window, stand at it, and look out for two minutes.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Put your shoes on. That is the whole first move.
tiers.done: you have been back inside with the door shut for one full minute.
tiers.test: to feel watched, and that standing there will feel ridiculous.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Walk to the end of your street and back.
tiers.why: Same street you already know. The deliberate intent is the whole difference.
tiers.alt: Walk to the nearest postbox or bin and back.
tiers.when: I next reach the corner of my own street
tiers.open: Walk to the first lamp post or gate and stop there.
tiers.done: you are back at your own door having turned round at the end of the street.
tiers.test: to be seen going nowhere and feel stupid about it.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Walk a full lap around the outside of your own building.
tiers.why: Most people have never seen all four sides of where they live.
tiers.alt: Walk your street on the pavement you never use.
tiers.when: I hear my front door shut behind me
tiers.open: Turn left out of your door instead of right.
tiers.done: you have passed your own front door again from the other side.
tiers.test: to find there is nothing to see and that the whole thing is pointless.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Walk your block in the opposite direction to habit.
tiers.why: Reversed, a known route stops being known. Cheapest new view there is.
tiers.alt: Take the stairs, back door, or side exit you never take.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Go out of your own door facing the direction you never face.
tiers.done: you have reached the point where the reversed route rejoins the one you know.
tiers.test: to get disoriented and feel foolish on your own street.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Turn down one street you have never turned down. One block, then home.
tiers.why: Novel geography starts one block from your door. It always did.
tiers.alt: Walk to the first corner you cannot picture, then turn back.
tiers.when: I next reach the corner of my own street
tiers.open: Stand at the corner and pick the turning you have never taken.
tiers.done: one block down it is behind you and you have turned for home.
tiers.test: to find it is a dead end, or someone's drive, and be embarrassed.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Stand in a public place for three minutes without touching your phone.
tiers.why: Being somewhere without a task is a skill. Start with three minutes.
tiers.alt: Sit outside your own front door for three phone-free minutes.
tiers.when: I am next standing at a stop or a platform
tiers.open: Put your phone in your pocket before you stop walking.
tiers.done: three minutes have passed without you taking your phone out.
tiers.test: to look like you are loitering and for someone to ask what you want.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Walk for fifteen minutes, choosing every turn at random.
tiers.why: No destination means you cannot arrive wrong.
tiers.alt: Walk ten minutes out in a straight line, then come back.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Walk to the end of the road and turn whichever way your body goes first.
tiers.done: fifteen minutes have passed with no route decided in advance.
tiers.test: to end up somewhere unpleasant and not know how to get back.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Walk to the furthest point you can reach in twenty minutes on foot.
tiers.why: Learn the real radius of your own legs. It is bigger than you think.
tiers.alt: Walk fifteen minutes out, then return by any other route.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Start a timer for twenty minutes and walk away from your door.
tiers.done: you have reached the twenty-minute mark and know where you are standing.
tiers.test: to run out of pavement, or energy, well before twenty minutes.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Take a completely different route to somewhere you go every week.
tiers.why: You have optimised that trip for years. Today, deliberately do it worse.
tiers.alt: Do a routine errand at an unfamiliar branch or location.
tiers.when: I pick my keys up to leave
tiers.open: Leave by a different exit, or turn the wrong way out of it, on purpose.
tiers.done: you have arrived at the usual place by a route you have never used.
tiers.test: to be late, and to resent having made the trip harder.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Sit on a public bench you have never sat on. Ten minutes.
tiers.why: Stillness in an unfamiliar spot. Nothing more is required.
tiers.alt: Stand and watch a street you never stop on for five minutes.
tiers.when: I next pass someone on the pavement
tiers.open: Sit down on the first unfamiliar bench you reach.
tiers.done: you have sat there for ten minutes without getting up early.
tiers.test: to be stared at for sitting still with no reason to be there.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Walk into a shop you have never entered. You do not have to buy anything.
tiers.why: Entering without a reason is the skill. Buying was always optional.
tiers.alt: Walk into a lobby, foyer, or courtyard you have only passed.
tiers.when: I next reach the front of a till
tiers.open: Push the door open and get yourself fully inside.
tiers.done: you have been inside long enough to look at one thing properly, and left.
tiers.test: to be approached by staff and have to explain why you came in.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.

tiers.do: Find the nearest green space you have never walked in.
tiers.why: There is one closer than you would guess. Go stand in it.
tiers.alt: Find a tree, garden, or waterway within a mile you cannot name.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Open a map, find the nearest green you cannot name, and start walking.
tiers.done: you are standing on grass you have never stood on.
tiers.test: to find it is small, fenced, or disappointing, and feel the trip was wasted.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Walk to a street whose name you do not know, then learn it.
tiers.why: Naming a place is how it joins your map.
tiers.alt: Photograph three street signs you have never read.
tiers.when: I next reach the corner of my own street
tiers.open: Keep going until you reach a sign you have never read, and read it.
tiers.done: you can say the street's name out loud without looking.
tiers.test: to realise you have lived here for years and known nothing.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Leave the house before 7am and walk for twenty minutes.
tiers.why: The same streets run on a different clock. Go see who else is up.
tiers.alt: Walk twenty minutes at the earliest hour you can manage today.
tiers.when: I turn my alarm off tomorrow
tiers.open: Get dressed before you let yourself check the time again.
tiers.done: you were outside and moving for twenty minutes before seven.
tiers.test: to be the only person out, and conspicuous for it.
tiers.stop: Not when you feel readier. Today's version is the task.

tiers.do: Walk somewhere after dark that you only ever go in daylight.
tiers.why: Familiar ground, unfamiliar light. Same place, new information.
tiers.alt: Walk a lit route you know at an hour you never walk it.
tiers.when: I turn the lights on this evening
tiers.open: Put your coat on while it is still light enough to leave.
tiers.done: you covered a route you know, in the dark, and came home.
tiers.test: to feel unsafe, and to turn back within a few minutes.
tiers.stop: No headphones. Hearing the place is part of it.

tiers.do: Walk one full mile in a direction you never travel.
tiers.why: Every compass point from your door except one is a habit.
tiers.alt: Walk twenty-five minutes down the road you always drive past.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Pick the compass direction you never go and take the first street that heads that way.
tiers.done: you have covered a mile in that one direction before turning back.
tiers.test: to find it is all the same, and that there was no point going.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Ride one stop past your usual and walk back.
tiers.why: The smallest possible act of overshooting. Learn how it feels.
tiers.alt: Walk one street past your usual turning, then loop back.
tiers.when: I next sit down on a bus or a train
tiers.open: Stay seated when the doors open at your stop.
tiers.done: you made your own way back from one stop past your own.
tiers.test: to misjudge it and end up much further out than you meant.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Get off two stops early and find a new way home.
tiers.why: You already know the way. Today you find a second one.
tiers.alt: Come home from an errand by a route you have never used.
tiers.when: I next sit down on a bus or a train
tiers.open: Press the button two stops before you normally would.
tiers.done: you are home by a route you had never used.
tiers.test: to get properly lost and arrive much later than planned.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Walk to the edge of your postcode and stand on the boundary.
tiers.why: Your invisible fence has a real location. Go touch it.
tiers.alt: Walk until the street names stop feeling like yours.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Look up where your postcode ends before you put your coat on.
tiers.done: you are standing on the boundary, and you know you are.
tiers.test: to find the edge is a dual carriageway, and the whole idea is silly.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Cross a bridge, tunnel, or crossing you have never crossed.
tiers.why: Barriers you never cross are the walls of the bubble.
tiers.alt: Cross to the far side of the biggest road near you and walk it.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Get to the crossing and look the whole way across it.
tiers.done: you have come back across it under your own power.
tiers.test: to feel exposed halfway across and want to turn round.
tiers.stop: No headphones. Hearing the place is part of it.

tiers.do: Take a bus you have never taken. Ride five stops.
tiers.why: You are collecting lines now, not destinations.
tiers.alt: Cycle or walk a route a bus you have never taken follows.
tiers.when: I am next standing at a stop or a platform
tiers.open: Get on the first service you have never taken, whichever comes.
tiers.done: you have ridden five stops and got off deliberately.
tiers.test: to end up somewhere you do not want to be, with no way back.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Visit the nearest place visitors go that you have never been.
tiers.why: Locals skip these on principle. The principle is costing you.
tiers.alt: Visit the landmark you have described but never entered.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Look up the opening time and write it on your hand.
tiers.done: you have been inside the place locals skip and stayed half an hour.
tiers.test: to feel like a tourist in your own town and be embarrassed.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Walk for one hour without checking a map.
tiers.why: Getting mildly lost within walking distance is entirely survivable.
tiers.alt: Walk thirty minutes with the map only for the way home.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Put your phone on aeroplane mode before you leave the house.
tiers.done: an hour has passed and you are walking home without having opened a map.
tiers.test: to get lost badly enough that it stops being funny.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Take a line you have never taken to its halfway point.
tiers.why: Nothing waits for you there. Go anyway.
tiers.alt: Cycle to a district you have never cycled through.
tiers.when: I am next standing at a stop or a platform
tiers.open: Buy the ticket to the halfway point before you decide anything else.
tiers.done: you have got off at the halfway stop and stood there for ten minutes.
tiers.test: to arrive somewhere with nothing in it and feel the day was wasted.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Spend an hour in a neighbourhood two districts from yours.
tiers.why: Two districts out is a different city with the same postcode.
tiers.alt: Spend an hour anywhere over an hour's walk from home.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Name the district out loud and start moving toward it.
tiers.done: you have spent a full hour there, not in transit to it.
tiers.test: to be obvious, and for people to clock that you are not from there.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Walk between two places you would normally take transport between.
tiers.why: The gap you always skip is where the city actually lives.
tiers.alt: Walk the last two kilometres of any journey today.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Leave your card at home so the bus stops being an option.
tiers.done: you have covered the whole gap on foot, including the part you always skip.
tiers.test: to find it takes far longer than it should and to regret it.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Find the highest publicly accessible point near you and go up it.
tiers.why: Seeing your own bubble from above changes its size.
tiers.alt: Get to the top floor of the tallest building you may enter.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Find the highest public point near you and set it as your only destination.
tiers.done: you can see your own area from above and have looked at it for five minutes.
tiers.test: to be turned away, or find it closed, and have made the trip for nothing.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Follow a river, canal, or coastline for an hour.
tiers.why: Water gives you a route that needs no decisions.
tiers.alt: Follow any single road for an hour without turning off it.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Walk to the water and turn so it is on your left.
tiers.done: you have followed it for a full hour without turning inland.
tiers.test: to get bored, and to find there is nothing to look at.
tiers.stop: No headphones. Hearing the place is part of it.

tiers.do: Eat a meal somewhere you have never eaten. Alone.
tiers.why: Sitting alone in an unfamiliar room is the whole exercise.
tiers.alt: Take food to an unfamiliar bench or square and eat it there.
tiers.when: I finish eating lunch tomorrow
tiers.open: Walk in and ask for a table for one, out loud.
tiers.done: you have eaten a whole meal there, sitting down, alone.
tiers.test: to be pitied, badly seated, or asked whether someone else is coming.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Take the slowest possible route somewhere you need to be.
tiers.why: Efficiency has been quietly shrinking your world.
tiers.alt: Add a twenty-minute detour to a trip you make anyway.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Choose the slowest option on the departure board, not the next one.
tiers.done: you have arrived where you needed to be by the slowest route available.
tiers.test: to be late, stressed, and to have ruined the day over nothing.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Spend an afternoon in a district you have never had a reason to visit.
tiers.why: No reason is the reason. Stay until your mental map redraws.
tiers.alt: Spend two hours in the district you have only driven through.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Put the district name in and start the journey before you read anything about it.
tiers.done: you have been there for a full afternoon and your sense of the place has changed.
tiers.test: to find it hostile or boring, and to feel the afternoon was thrown away.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Ride to the last stop on a line. Walk for an hour from there.
tiers.why: The end of the line is where the city stops performing.
tiers.alt: Ride or cycle to the outer edge of the network and walk back in.
tiers.when: I am next standing at a stop or a platform
tiers.open: Stay on past the last stop you recognise.
tiers.done: you are an hour's walk from the end of the line, on foot.
tiers.test: to be stranded at the edge of the network after dark.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Visit an industrial, agricultural, or unglamorous edge of where you live.
tiers.why: The parts nobody photographs are still part of your world.
tiers.alt: Walk a working district — depots, yards, wholesale markets.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Head for the depots and the yards rather than the centre.
tiers.done: you have spent two hours in the part nobody photographs.
tiers.test: to be obviously out of place, and challenged about why you are there.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Use a mode of transport you have not used in five years.
tiers.why: Your body remembers more than your confidence does.
tiers.alt: Borrow or hire a bike, scooter, or boat for an hour.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find where to hire or borrow it and make the enquiry today.
tiers.done: you have used it for an hour, badly, in public.
tiers.test: to be visibly incompetent at something you used to do easily.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.

tiers.do: Spend three hours somewhere with no plan and no phone map.
tiers.why: Unstructured time in an unfamiliar place is the actual muscle.
tiers.alt: Spend ninety minutes somewhere new with your phone in your bag.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Put your phone in your bag, zipped, before you leave the house.
tiers.done: three hours have passed somewhere unfamiliar with no plan and no map.
tiers.test: to run out of things to do within an hour and feel pointless.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Enter a public building you have never entered — library, gallery, hall.
tiers.why: Public means yours. You have been acting like a guest.
tiers.alt: Sit in a public reading room or foyer for half an hour.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Walk through the main door as though you belong there, because you do.
tiers.done: you have sat down inside a public building you had never entered.
tiers.test: to be stopped and asked what you are here for.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.
tiers.say: "Is it alright if I sit in here for a bit?"

tiers.do: Walk ten kilometres in one go.
tiers.why: Distance on foot rewrites what counts as 'near'.
tiers.alt: Walk seven kilometres, or cycle twenty.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Eat something and fill a bottle before you decide the route.
tiers.done: ten kilometres are behind you in one continuous go.
tiers.test: to have to stop at five and admit you could not do it.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Find the oldest street where you live and walk its full length.
tiers.why: Depth is a direction too. Your bubble has a history.
tiers.alt: Walk the full length of your longest local road.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Look up which street is oldest and go to one end of it.
tiers.done: you covered it end to end without cutting any of it out.
tiers.test: to find it is just a road, and that the history is invisible.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Cross into the next town on foot or by bike.
tiers.why: Arriving under your own power changes what arriving means.
tiers.alt: Reach the next town by the slowest transport available.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Fill a bottle and put it by the door tonight.
tiers.done: you have crossed into the next town under your own power.
tiers.test: to run out before the boundary and have to get transport home.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Go somewhere solely because you cannot picture it.
tiers.why: Unimaginable is the only selection criterion from here on. Do not look it up before you go.
tiers.alt: Pick a name off a map you cannot visualise and go.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Open a map, pick a name you cannot picture, and say it out loud.
tiers.done: you have been there, and it is no longer a name you cannot picture.
tiers.test: to find there is nothing there, and that unimaginable just meant dull.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Take a train to a town you cannot state one fact about. Four hours there.
tiers.why: Do not research it before you go. Ignorance is the point.
tiers.alt: Drive or cycle to a town you know nothing about and stay three hours.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Book the ticket now, before you look the town up.
tiers.done: you have spent four hours there and can state one real thing about it.
tiers.test: to be bored for four hours with nowhere to sit and nothing to see.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Spend an entire day outside the city or town you live in.
tiers.why: A full day elsewhere resets more than an afternoon ever will.
tiers.alt: Spend six hours beyond your usual limits, however you get there.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Put one date in your calendar tonight and block the whole day.
tiers.done: a full day has passed with you outside your own town.
tiers.test: to want to come back by lunchtime and to have wasted the fare.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Go somewhere the accent, dialect, or language is not yours.
tiers.why: Being slightly hard to understand is good practice.
tiers.alt: Spend an afternoon in a community whose first language differs.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find where that community gathers near you and pick a day.
tiers.done: you have spent an afternoon somewhere your accent is the unusual one.
tiers.test: to be unable to understand anyone and to feel like an intruder.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Navigate a full day by paper map, signage, or memory only.
tiers.why: You had this ability before. Get it back.
tiers.alt: Navigate half a day with no live directions.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Print or buy one paper map tonight and put your phone in a drawer.
tiers.done: a whole day has passed navigated on signage, paper and memory alone.
tiers.test: to get badly lost and lose hours you could not afford.
tiers.stop: Map stays in your pocket. Getting it slightly wrong is included.

tiers.do: Take a ferry, tram, cable car, or regional line you have never taken.
tiers.why: New vehicles teach you the shape of a place faster than maps.
tiers.alt: Take the least convenient scheduled transport out of town.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Look up the timetable and buy the ticket for a specific sailing.
tiers.done: you have travelled on it and arrived somewhere you had not been.
tiers.test: to find it slow, uncomfortable, and not worth the fare.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Travel twenty-five kilometres from home under your own power and back.
tiers.why: Your own legs, that far out. Remember the number.
tiers.alt: Walk a half-marathon distance across a single day.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Check the tyres and fill two bottles before you look at the route.
tiers.done: you have covered fifty kilometres out and back under your own power.
tiers.test: to break down, or break, twenty kilometres from home.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Visit the nearest coast, mountain, or wilderness you have never seen.
tiers.why: Terrain you cannot control is worth standing in.
tiers.alt: Reach the largest piece of open country within reach today.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the nearest piece of real country and put one date against it.
tiers.done: you have stood in terrain that nobody arranged for you.
tiers.test: to find it uncomfortable, cold, and worse than the photographs.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Go to a market, festival, or gathering of a community not your own.
tiers.why: Be the guest for an afternoon. Buy something. Say thank you.
tiers.alt: Attend any public event where you will be in a clear minority.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find one gathering on a date you could actually make, and write the date down.
tiers.done: you have been, bought something, and said thank you to the person who sold it.
tiers.test: to be unwelcome, obviously the outsider, and asked why you came.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.
tiers.say: "Can you tell me what this one is?"

tiers.do: Spend a full day with no destination chosen before you leave.
tiers.why: Decide from the road. The road is better informed than you were.
tiers.alt: Leave with only the first leg decided and improvise the rest.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Set your alarm and decide nothing else tonight.
tiers.done: a full day has gone by with every destination chosen after you left.
tiers.test: to freeze at the station, pick nothing, and go home.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Reach a place that takes three changes of transport to get to.
tiers.why: Friction of transit is the toll on a bigger world. Pay it once.
tiers.alt: Reach somewhere that takes over three hours to get to.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Work out the three changes on paper and book only the first.
tiers.done: you have arrived somewhere that took three changes to reach.
tiers.test: to miss a connection and be stuck between two places.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Sleep one night away from home. Anywhere.
tiers.why: Waking somewhere unfamiliar resets more than any day trip.
tiers.alt: Spend a night at a friend's, a hostel, or a campsite nearby.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Message one person tonight and ask if you can stay, or book the cheapest bed you can find.
tiers.done: you have woken up somewhere that is not your home.
tiers.test: to lie awake all night and want to come home at two in the morning.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Wake somewhere new and walk for an hour before you eat.
tiers.why: The first hour in an unknown place is the most honest one.
tiers.alt: On any night away, walk an unfamiliar area at first light.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Put your shoes by the bed before you sleep.
tiers.done: an hour of moving through an unfamiliar place is behind you, before you ate anything.
tiers.test: to feel lost and exposed walking somewhere you do not know at dawn.

tiers.do: Two days away, alone, under a hundred kilometres.

tiers.do: Go somewhere with nowhere to sleep booked until you arrive.

tiers.do: Spend a night somewhere with fewer than five thousand people.

tiers.do: Spend a night in a city several times the size of yours.

tiers.done: you slept there and covered it the next morning.
tiers.test: to be overwhelmed within an hour and hide in the room.

tiers.do: Take an overnight train, bus, or ferry.

tiers.done: you have woken up somewhere you went to sleep travelling toward.

tiers.do: Travel for a full day in one direction and stop where you stop.
tiers.why: No target means no failure. Just distance and daylight.

tiers.done: a full day of travelling in one direction has ended wherever it ended.
tiers.test: to end up somewhere with no bed and no way onward.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Enter a country, region, or state you have never entered.
tiers.why: A line on a map you have never crossed is a wall you built.

tiers.done: you have crossed a border you had never crossed.
tiers.test: to be stopped, questioned, or turned back at the line.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Spend a weekend somewhere chosen by opening a map at random.
tiers.why: Let chance pick. Your preferences are what kept the bubble small.
tiers.alt: Let someone else pick your destination and go without asking why.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day

tiers.done: you spent the weekend where chance put you, not where you would have chosen.
tiers.test: to land somewhere awful and spend two days regretting the method.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Three days in a city where you know nobody.
tiers.why: No safety net of familiar faces. Just you and the streets.

tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Book three nights somewhere you cannot name one person in.
tiers.done: three days have passed with no familiar face in them.
tiers.test: to speak to nobody for three days and feel it confirm something.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Travel for four days with hand luggage only.
tiers.why: Everything you own is optional. Prove it for four days.
tiers.alt: Travel for two days with only what fits in a daypack.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Pack the bag tonight. Whatever does not fit is not coming.
tiers.done: four days are done and you never opened a second bag.
tiers.test: to need something you left behind and be stuck without it.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Spend three days somewhere with no return ticket booked.
tiers.why: The unbooked return changes how you spend every hour.

tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day

tiers.done: three days passed with the return still unbooked when you set off.
tiers.test: to be unable to get home when you want to, or to pay far more.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Go somewhere whose name you cannot pronounce. Stay two nights.
tiers.why: You will learn to say it. That is how places become yours.
tiers.alt: Pick the least familiar name on the departures board and go.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day

tiers.done: you can pronounce it, and you have slept there twice.
tiers.test: to mispronounce it to someone's face and be corrected or laughed at.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.

tiers.do: Spend four days somewhere you cannot read the signage.
tiers.why: Illiteracy is temporary and instructive. Navigate by pattern.

tiers.done: four days have passed navigating by shape, number and guess.
tiers.test: to get something badly wrong because you could not read a warning.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Travel alone for five days with nothing planned past the first night.
tiers.why: Five days of your own company, deciding as you go.

tiers.done: five days alone are behind you, with only the first one planned.
tiers.test: to run out of nerve on day two and book a flight home.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Take a single journey lasting more than eight hours.

tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Stay two nights somewhere with no private room.

tiers.done: you have slept two nights in a room with strangers in it.
tiers.test: to be unable to sleep, and to have nowhere to be alone.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.test: to be homesick by day three and count the days down.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: One week somewhere you cannot read the signage.
tiers.why: Seven days navigating by nerve and pattern. You will manage.

tiers.done: a week has passed with every sign a guess.
tiers.test: to make a serious mistake because you could not read something.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Spend a week in a climate unlike anywhere you have lived.

tiers.open: Look up what the weather actually is there, then book a week.
tiers.done: a week has passed in air your body has never breathed.
tiers.test: to be ill, uncomfortable, or unable to cope with the climate.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Ten days away with no itinerary past the first night.

tiers.done: ten days are behind you and nine of them were decided on the ground.
tiers.test: to waste days deciding and get nowhere at all.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.done: a week has passed using only what the people who live there use.
tiers.test: to be refused, overcharged, or obviously an intruder.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Cross a border on foot, by bike, or by boat.

tiers.done: you have crossed a border on foot, by bike or by boat.
tiers.test: to be held at the crossing, or refused for the wrong paperwork.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Spend two weeks away from home.

tiers.test: to be desperate to come home by the end of the first week.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Go somewhere that requires a visa, permit, or vaccination.

tiers.test: to be refused, and for the refusal to settle the matter for good.
tiers.stop: Not when you feel readier. Today's version is the task.

tiers.do: Spend three days somewhere with no reliable signal.
tiers.why: Unreachable for three days. The world will hold.

tiers.done: three days have passed with nobody able to reach you.
tiers.test: for something to go wrong at home while you are unreachable.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Two weeks in a country whose language you do not speak.

tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Spend two months in a country you had never considered.

tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.
